ops.title: Tailscale SSH on the yclaw fleet swallows remote exit codes (false → rc=0) — decide remote state from output, never rc; admin's remote shell is zsh with fatal nomatch globs
ops.body:
Verified live 2026-07-08 against metal (tailscaled 1.98.5): the Tailscale SSH server does NOT
propagate remote command exit codes. `ssh admin@metal false`, `ssh root@metal false`,
`ssh -tt admin@metal false`, and `tailscale ssh admin@metal -- false` ALL return rc=0.
Connection-level failures (check wall, unreachable) still fail properly with rc 255.

**Why:** any script branching on a remote command's exit status over Tailscale SSH silently
takes the success path — e.g. onboard.sh's original `gemini_logged_in` (remote `grep -q` rc)
would have reported "already logged in" with no token present and skipped the login gate.

**How to apply:** decide remote state CLIENT-side from command output (print a marker/list and
grep locally), never from ssh's rc. Also: remote shell differs by user — admin gets zsh (login
shell, fatal `no matches found` on unmatched globs), root gets /bin/sh (unmatched glob falls
through literally). Suppress remote-shell stderr client-side. Fixed pattern lives in
scripts/onboard.sh `cliproxy_auth_files` (output over the wire) + `gemini_logged_in` (client-side
grep of that output). Related: [[metal-vm-service-commands]], [[deploy-pipeline-fixes-2026-06]].
